narrative:
On August 31, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 44.6%, with 960 cases heard out of 2,153 scheduled. This performance reflects a steady daily increase in overall judicial clearance efficiency, rising from 43.8% on August 29, 42.2% on August 28, and 37.7% on August 27. 

Individual judge listings revealed stark differences in case management. Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty in Court Hall 19 processed the day’s largest docket, hearing 125 of 227 scheduled matters (55.1%). High conversion rates were also achieved by Justice Chillakur Sumalatha, who heard 60 of 77 scheduled cases (77.9%), and Justice S. Rachaiah, who processed 41 of 56 cases (73.2%). Conversely, listings under Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad in Court Hall 6 saw none of his 190 scheduled cases heard.

An analysis of hearing stages indicates that procedural and early-stage matters progressed most efficiently. The "Orders" stage saw the highest activity, converting 394 of 712 scheduled cases (55.3%), while "Admission" and "Preliminary Hearing" converted at 41.0% and 40.0% respectively. "Final Hearing" stages, which traditionally demand deeper arguments, saw the lowest conversion rate at 27.1% (107 of 395 scheduled cases).

In terms of case-type distribution, Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the roster with 995 scheduled cases, achieving a 42.4% hearing rate—an improvement from the 37.9% recorded on August 29. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) comprised 296 scheduled cases but saw their clearance rate decline to 39.5% from a high of 61.9% on August 29. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) maintained robust progress, with 84 of 167 scheduled cases heard (50.3%).
